title: GRACE FOR THE ONE WHO SERVES

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is a lasting ordinance for them. The man who sprinkles the water of cleansing must also wash his clothes, and anyone who touches the water of cleansing will be unclean till evening. Anything that an unclean person touches becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it becomes unclean till evening." — Num 19:21-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes by returning to a theme we noticed earlier: even the one who applied the cleansing water became unclean in the process. Handling the means of others' purity carried a cost. There is a quiet, repeated reminder here that serving in holy things and helping others toward cleanness was never without personal impact.

This final note keeps us humble. No one in this whole system was above the reach of defilement. The very man doing the cleansing needed cleansing himself. It underscores how thorough and pervasive uncleanness was, and how everyone, even the servant of the ritual, stood in need of grace. There was no human figure in this system who was untouched, pure enough to cleanse others without needing cleansing themselves.

That very limitation points us to our need for a greater cleanser. Every priest, every helper, every person in this chapter was themselves in need of purity. The whole system, for all its beauty, could not produce a truly clean mediator. It could only keep pointing forward, waiting for one who could cleanse others without being defiled Himself.

And that One has come. Jesus alone touches our uncleanness without being defiled. He alone cleanses others while remaining perfectly pure. Where every servant in this chapter needed washing, Christ needed none — the spotless one who makes the unclean clean. He is the mediator this whole system longed for, the pure one who can truly purify us. The book of Hebrews says it plainly: the blood of Christ will "cleanse our consciences" in a way no ceremony ever could. Rest in Him, the only one who cleanses fully and is never Himself defiled.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Why is it significant that everyone in this system needed cleansing?
2. How does this point to your need for a perfect, undefiled cleanser?
3. What comfort do you find in Christ, who purifies you while remaining pure?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that this whole system pointed to my need for Jesus, the only one who cleanses others while remaining perfectly pure. Cleanse my conscience by His blood, and let me rest in the one who purifies me completely. Amen.
